title: Finite lifted generator covers and a test for quasi-separated objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a coherent Grothendieck topos [def-trf-coherent-topos] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and fix a small full generating subcategory $\mathcal G$ of coherent objects closed under finite limits. Generating means that every object admits an epimorphism from a coproduct of members of $\mathcal G$; a family is jointly epimorphic if its coproduct map is an epimorphism, and epimorphism means right cancellation. Then:
(1) For every epimorphism $e:E\to X$ with $X$ quasi-compact there are a finite set $I$, objects $G_i\in\mathcal G$, and maps $u_i:G_i\to X$, $v_i:G_i\to E$ such that $e v_i=u_i$ and $(u_i)_i$ is jointly epimorphic. In particular every quasi-compact object has a finite jointly epimorphic family from $\mathcal G$. The set $I$ may be empty.
(2) Let $p:P\to A$ be any epimorphism. Then $A$ is quasi-separated if and only if, for every $K,L\in\mathcal G$ and every $k:K\to P$, $l:L\to P$, the object $K\times_A L$, formed with the maps $pk$ and $pl$, is quasi-compact. Here quasi-separated means that $B\times_A C$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact $B,C$ with maps to $A$, as in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. There is no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption on $P$ or $A$.

Context: literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 178–179.

proof.text: For (1), choose a small jointly epimorphic family $(w_j:G_j\to E)_{j\in J}$ from $\mathcal G$, using the generating hypothesis. Its composite family $(e w_j:G_j\to X)_j$ is jointly epimorphic: if $a,b:X\to T$ agree after every $e w_j$, the coproduct universal property and epimorphy of $\coprod_jG_j\to E$ give $ae=be$, and epimorphy of $e$ gives $a=b$. Quasi-compactness of $X$, by [def-trf-coherent-topos], selects a finite subset $I\subseteq J$ whose composite family is still jointly epimorphic. Set $v_i=w_i$ and $u_i=e w_i$. Restriction does not change these equalities, so the selected maps retain their lifts. Applying this construction with $e=\operatorname{id}_X$ proves the particular assertion. No nonemptiness was used: $I=\varnothing$ is allowed by the same quasi-compactness definition.

source.place: Tag 0D07 (definition-quasi-compact-topos); finite-subfamily selection from a generating epimorphism. Agent argument for this auxiliary.

proof.text: For the forward implication of (2), suppose $A$ is quasi-separated. Each $K,L\in\mathcal G$ is coherent and hence quasi-compact by [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Apply the definition of quasi-separatedness to these two quasi-compact objects and the maps $pk:K\to A$, $pl:L\to A$. It gives quasi-compactness of $K\times_A L$. This direction does not require epimorphy of $p$.

source.place: Agent specialization of def-trf-coherent-topos to two members of the coherent generating subcategory.

proof.text: For the reverse implication, assume the stated test for all $K,L,k,l$. Fix arbitrary quasi-compact objects $B,C$ with maps $b:B\to A$, $c:C\to A$. By clause (1) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus], pulling back the epimorphism $p$ gives epimorphisms $q_B:B\times_A P\to B$ and $q_C:C\times_A P\to C$. Apply the finite lifted-cover construction of step 1 to each of $q_B,q_C$. Obtain finite jointly epimorphic families $s_i:K_i\to B$ and $t_j:L_j\to C$ from $\mathcal G$, with lifts $\widetilde s_i:K_i\to B\times_A P$ and $\widetilde t_j:L_j\to C\times_A P$. Their second projections $k_i:K_i\to P$ and $l_j:L_j\to P$ satisfy $pk_i=bs_i$ and $pl_j=ct_j$ by the defining pullback equations. Quasi-compactness is needed only for $B,C$, not for either pullback or for $P$.

source.place: Agent pullback argument using clause (1) of lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus (sheaf epimorphism/local-lifting calculus, Tags 00WN and 00W2), followed by step 1.

proof.text: The assumed test applied to $k_i,l_j$ says that every $K_i\times_A L_j$ is quasi-compact; its maps to $A$ are precisely $bs_i,ct_j$ by step 3. The product-family assertion in clause (1) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus] makes $(K_i\times_A L_j\to B\times_A C)_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$ jointly epimorphic. Its index set is finite, so clause (3) of that node makes $B\times_A C$ quasi-compact. Clause (3) explicitly includes an empty finite family, so the conclusion still holds if either cover is empty. Since $B,C,b,c$ were arbitrary, [def-trf-coherent-topos] now says that $A$ is quasi-separated. No finiteness property of $A$ or $P$ has been assumed.
